summary: Onboarding: mutual-TLS SFTP SIEM sink (gzipped NDJSON) + signed-manifest + certificate-rotation evidence + SIG-Lite questionnaire
description:
Issue summary:
Customer FinX Payments is onboarding a production SIEM sink that requires: (1) push delivery to their SFTP endpoint over mutual-TLS with client certificate authentication, (2) payloads as gzipped NDJSON batches, (3) a per-batch signed manifest (ed25519) and per-record deterministic pseudonymization tokens to support GDPR deletion requests, and (4) accompanying evidence for their vendor security review (SIG-Lite) and SOC2 artifacts.

Impact:
FinX is unable to complete their compliance onboarding; they have a deadline for an audit window the week of 2026-03-22. Until we deliver the requested export format and rotation proof they cannot validate chain-of-custody for audit. This blocks go-live for several production workloads.

Environment:
- Redwood prod - us-east export pipeline
- Customer SFTP endpoint: sftp.finx-payments.com:22 (mutual TLS expected)
- Export config requested: daily incremental batches (UTC midnight), gzipped ndjson (.ndjson.gz), ed25519 manifest (manifest.json.sig) per-batch

Customer asks / Deliverables requested:
1) Console configuration snippet / API payload example to create a mutual-TLS SFTP sink that supports file uploads with client cert authentication and server cert verification.
2) Example exported bundle (one small sample day) containing gzipped NDJSON, signed manifest, and mapping CSV that maps Redwood audit fields to FinX SIEM fields.
3) Proof of client certificate rotation process and rotation logs from Redwood side: signed rotation manifest showing previous cert fingerprint -> new cert fingerprint with timestamps, and how Redwood validates the customer-provided CA chain.
4) Explanation of per-record GDPR deletion token generation (deterministic, keyed-hash approach) and how to map deletion tokens back to originals for legal SARs.
5) Completed SIG-Lite (attached spreadsheet) with answers and pointers to SOC2 artifacts.
6) Recommended PII sampling/redaction template for gzipped NDJSON (which fields we pseudonymize by default and which are delivered hashed), and retention controls.

Attachments from customer:
- SIG-Lite spreadsheet (FinX_SIG-Lite_v2.xlsx)
- Example SFTP host key and expected CN pattern for client certs

Priority & deadline:
Customer requests first deliverable (console snippet + sample bundle) by 2026-03-12 to satisfy vendor review before audit window.

Notes on security expectations:
- Customer requires manifest signatures to be verifiable via ed25519 public key they control. They also request per-batch HMAC for delivery receipts.
- All artifacts must demonstrate non-repudiation and provide resume tokens for incremental replay.

Desired outcome:
Provide step-by-step onboarding runbook + sample bundle + rotation proof + completed SIG-Lite answers so FinX can finish their vendor security checklist and proceed with production onboarding.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) In Console > Integrations > SIEM Sink, choose SFTP and paste sftp.finx-payments.com:22 with client-cert auth enabled.
2) Upload client cert (PEM) and private key for Redwood to use when connecting.
3) Configure payload format: ndjson.gz, daily, manifest signature ed25519.
4) Click Test Connection => observed 'TLS handshake failure: client cert rejected' in UI (what customer reported).
5) Attempt to push sample bundle via API -> server returns 403 Manifest verification failed (customer claim).

comments: 2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel: Opened ticket after initial FinX support call. Attached SIG-Lite template. Customer provided example host details and asked for sample bundle.
2026-03-11 - Jordan Kim (Support): Thank you — starting investigation. Assigning to SRE for mTLS logs and to Data-Export for manifest/format sample. cc @sre-oncall #support.

2026-03-11 - SRE (Miguel Santos): Preliminary finding: client cert presented but chain not trusted by customer's SFTP endpoint; CN pattern mismatch noted. Asking customer for their CA bundle and exact allowed CN wildcard. (Slack: #support / thread 'finx-mtls')

2026-03-12 - Data Export (Leah Chen): Working on sample bundle generator. Need to confirm deterministic pseudonymization salt handling for their legal mapping. Proposed approach: HKDF-SHA256 with tenant salt stored in KMS. Please confirm customer accepts KMS-sourced salt rather than customer-supplied salt.

2026-03-13 - FinX Security (Marcus Li): Provided CA bundle and acceptance of KMS-provided salt. Also attached requested SOC2 cover letter reference FINX-2025. Requested that rotation logs be signed and include timestamped fingerprints. Waiting on sample bundle.
investigation_notes:
SRE checked TLS logs: client cert presented by upload-worker-3 matched fingerprint f3:4a:...; customer's sftp logging rejects due to CA not in truststore.
Action: request customer's CA and add to temporary allowlist for test connection.

Manifest verification failure trace: signature header missing 'x-manifest-signature' in our sample; upload-worker omitted header when Content-Encoding was gzip. Hypothesis: Content-Encoding header suppressed by proxy leading to signature mismatch.
Action: Reproduce locally with sftp proxy and ensure headers preserved for signature calculation.

Pseudonymization design: Implement deterministic token = base64url(HKDF-SHA256(tenant_kms_key, subject_id || date)[:16]) with rotation window documented. Store mapping only when customer requests retrieval for SARs; otherwise mapping not retained to minimize PII footprint. Need legal approval before shipping mapping behavior.

Handover items for Engineering: small patch to upload-worker to preserve signature header when gzipping payloads; unit tests added in PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/siem-connectors/pull/4521
resolution: Pending - awaiting customer's CA bundle confirmation (received 2026-03-13) and Security sign-off on pseudonymization mapping. Next steps: schedule test window with FinX on 2026-03-15 and provide sample bundle and completed SIG-Lite answers. Will attach signed rotation manifest after engineering runs rotation proof job.

2) Run test connection with customer's CA bundle in temporary allowlist and confirm mutual TLS handshake (owner: SRE, scheduled 2026-03-15)

6) Post-resolution: follow-up ticket to instrument audit of exports for non-repudiation and to add an automated delivery receipt mechanism (owner: Platform)
